The A-Buffer Visibility Pass is a GPU fragment-stage algorithm that generates an approximate visibility function $\tilde{v}(x_e, x)$ for each view ray by storing depth and visibility control points in an A-Buffer [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states in Section 5.2 and the notes that the A-Buffer Visibility Pass is a GPU fragment-stage algorithm. It confirms that it generates an approximate visibility function $	ilde{v}(x_e, x)$ for each view ray and stores depth ($d$) and visibility ($v$) control points in an A-Buffer (described as a 2D texture array).

The merging process adds overhead when the buffer is full, potentially increasing complexity depending on the number of merges required [S1, unofficial].

The evidence supports the claim that a merging process occurs when the buffer is full and that this process involves decimating control points (removing the one with the smallest difference). However, the evidence does not explicitly state that this process 'adds overhead' or 'increases complexity'. While it mentions that using peak finding 'increases computation time', it does not quantify the overhead or complexity impact of the merging process itself, nor does it link the complexity increase to the 'number of merges required'. Therefore, only part of the claim is supported.
